sources.title: US has no immediate plan to strike Iran, Trump tells FT
CVS Health to break up into two companies, WSJ reports
Hong Kong Q3 GDP expands by 5.2% year-on-year, outlook positive

stories.headline: Trump says no immediate US strike planned against Iran
stories.body: Reuters reported President Donald Trump told the Financial Times the United States had no immediate plans to strike Iran. The report did not establish a formal ceasefire or peace agreement.
stories.analysis: Potential short-term geopolitical de-escalation signal, but insufficient to infer a specific oil-price or interest-rate reaction.
stories.watch_next: Formal US statement, Iran response and any confirmed progress in negotiations.

stories.headline: CVS Health reportedly plans to separate pharmacy and insurance businesses
stories.body: Reuters reported that, according to the Wall Street Journal, CVS Health would split into two businesses separating retail pharmacies from insurance and pharmacy-benefit operations. CVS had not immediately responded to Reuters for confirmation.
stories.analysis: Potential changes to debt allocation and credit risk profiles across the resulting issuers.
stories.watch_next: Official CVS confirmation, debt allocation, transaction terms and guidance.

stories.headline: Hong Kong third-quarter GDP exceeds Reuters-polled expectations
stories.body: Hong Kong third-quarter GDP expanded 5.2% year over year, ahead of a 3.6% Reuters-polled forecast. Total goods exports increased 30.4% year over year.
stories.analysis: Indicates stronger regional export activity; does not establish a change to MAS policy or USD/SGD.
stories.watch_next: GDP revisions, export momentum, and regional demand resilience.
